q: 1. A good building stone should not absorb water more than ............
explain: For a stone to be considered high quality for construction, its water absorption should be less than 5% by weight. Above 10%, the stone is generally rejected.

q: 2. Which of the following has more fire resisting characteristics?
explain: Compact sandstone is better at resisting fire compared to others because its grain structure doesn't disintegrate as easily under high heat as marble or granite.

q: 3. Jumper is a tool used for ............
explain: A jumper is a long steel bar used in quarrying to drill deep holes in rocks for blasting.

q: 4. Gneiss is chemically classified as ............
explain: Gneiss is a silicious rock as its main constituent is silica (quartz). It is formed by the metamorphosis of granite.

q: 5. The cracks which extend from bark towards the sap wood in the cross section of a tree, are called ............
explain: Star shakes are cracks that extend from the bark towards the sapwood. They are usually caused by severe frost or extreme heat during the growth of the tree.

q: 6. Sea sand used in structures causes ............
explain: Sea sand contains hygroscopic salts that absorb moisture (dampness), crystallize on surfaces (efflorescence), and can lead to the corrosion of reinforcement and general disintegration.

q: 7. The property due to which steel can withstand hammer blows is called ............
explain: Toughness is the ability of a material to absorb energy and withstand impact or shock loads without fracturing.

q: 8. Laterite is a/an ............
explain: Laterite is an argillaceous rock because it contains a high percentage of clay (alumina) alongside iron oxides.

q: 9. Crushing strength of good building stone should be more than ............
explain: For a stone to be used in major structural work, its crushing strength should ideally exceed 100 MPa (1000 kg/cm²).

q: 10. Chlorite a green colour mineral is mainly derived from the decomposition of ............
explain: As Per Book Key A. But as per Google Chlorite is a secondary mineral formed from the alteration (weathering/decomposition) of various ferromagnesian minerals like biotite or hornblende.

q: 11. Most of the stones possess the specific gravity in the range of ............
explain: Building stones generally have a density between 2400 and 2800 kg/m³, resulting in a specific gravity between 2.4 and 2.8.

q: 12. The sub-classification of sedimentary rocks ...............
explain: Sedimentary rocks are classified based on their mode of formation: mechanically formed (sandstone), chemically formed (gypsum), or organically formed (limestone).

q: 13. The tendency of the minerals to split along a certain plane is called ...............
explain: Cleavage is the tendency of a mineral to break along flat, parallel planes of weakness in its crystalline structure.

q: 14. The fracture in asbestos is ...............
explain: Asbestos is naturally a fibrous mineral; when broken, it separates into long, thin, flexible fibers.

q: 15. Granite is mainly composed of ...............
explain: Granite is an igneous rock primarily composed of Quartz,Feldspar and Mica  as a mineral.

q: 16. In order to dry the quarry sap of a freshly quarried stone, it should be exposed to open air for a period of ...............
explain: Proper seasoning of stone involves allowing the 'quarry sap' to evaporate, which typically takes 6 to 12 months to ensure the stone is hard and durable.

q: 17. Which of the following sedimentary rocks changes into quartzite by metamorphic action?
explain: Under intense heat and pressure (metamorphism), the quartz grains in sandstone fuse together to form quartzite.

q: 18. Slate is formed by metamorphic action on ............
explain: Slate is a fine-grained, foliated metamorphic rock created by the alteration of shale or mudstone by low-grade regional metamorphism.

q: 19. Pegmatite is an example of ..........
explain: Pegmatite is a coarse-textured igneous rock that forms during the final stages of a magma's crystallization deep underground.

q: 20. Hard silicious rocks which cannot be scratched by a knife represent a hardness of .............
explain: A common steel knife blade has a hardness of about 5.5 to 6. Hard silicious rocks like quartz have a hardness of 7 and cannot be scratched by a knife.

q: 21. Stainless steel contains .............
explain: The most common grade of stainless steel (18/8 stainless) contains approximately 18% chromium and 8% nickel.

q: 22. The cast iron when heated to red heat with powder red haemetite in an oven for increasing its toughness converted to ............
explain: This process (annealing with an oxidizing agent like haematite) reduces the carbon content, turning brittle cast iron into tougher, malleable 'Motteled' iron.

q: 23. In which of the following directions, the strength of timber is maximum?
explain: Timber is strongest along its fibers; compressive and tensile strengths are significantly higher when applied parallel to the grain direction.

q: 24. The fuel generally used for burning limestone is ............
explain: Limestone can be calcined in kilns using various fuels depending on availability and the type of kiln (intermittent or continuous).

q: 25. The arrangement, size and shape of the constituent mineral grains of a stone gives the information about its ............
explain: Texture refers specifically to the physical appearance of the rock based on the size, shape, and arrangement of its grains.

q: 26. The rocks which are formed due to pouring of magma at the earth's surface are called ........
explain: Volcanic rocks (like basalt) form from lava cooling rapidly on the surface, resulting in very small crystals.

q: 27. The quarrying of stone by the method of wedging is successfully carried out in ............
explain: Wedging is effective for sedimentary and metamorphic rocks that have natural bedding planes or cleavage, such as sandstone, limestone, and marble.

q: 28. Pegmatite is a/an ............
explain: Pegmatite is an intrusive igneous rock characterized by very large interlocking crystals, usually formed during the final stages of magma crystallization.

q: 29. The yield strength and tensile strength of low carbon steel may be improved by the addition of ............
explain: As per Key D is answer but as per google Manganese increases the strength and hardness of steel and acts as a deoxidizer during the manufacturing process.

q: 30. The rock with poorest strength is ............
explain: Shale is a fine-grained, clastic sedimentary rock with a laminated structure that makes it weak and easily split.

q: 31. Geologically, marble is known as ............
explain: Marble is a metamorphic rock formed when limestone is subjected to the heat and pressure of metamorphism.

q: 32. Sand stone is ............
explain: Sandstone is a classic sedimentary rock composed mainly of sand-sized mineral particles or rock fragments.

q: 33. Lime stone is not a ............
explain: Limestone is sedimentary, stratified, and aqueous. It only becomes metamorphic (marble) after transformation under heat and pressure.

q: 34. The rocks having alumina or clay as their major constituents, are known as ............
explain: Argillaceous rocks are a class of sedimentary rocks defined by having a high proportion of clay minerals or alumina.
